title_en: Playing for Scale: The Future of Sports Investing
title_zh: 为规模而赛：体育投资的未来 —— 对话 Goldman Sachs 的 Nicole Polon-Ross
subtitle_zh: 媒体版权与机构资本点燃体育投资热潮，聊球队估值、场馆融资、大学体育与女子联赛的机会。
description: Playing for Scale: The Future of Sports Investing

turns.en: Ultimately, every investor in a sports team is most interested in winning, and so all of the investment that they can make that will help the team become more valuable allows them to invest more in their players and increase their opportunity for winning. A record price for a minority stake in a major basketball franchise.
turns.zh: 归根结底，一支运动队的每一位投资者最在意的都是赢球，所以他们能做的、有助于让球队变得更值钱的所有投资，都能让他们在球员身上投入更多、增加赢球的机会。一支顶级篮球球队（franchise）的少数股权（minority stake）拍出了创纪录的价格。

turns.en: A multi-dillion dollar investment in one of baseball's most iconic organizations, the first billion dollar franchise in women's professional sports, and a final quarter-prooval of a landmark settlement that will allow college athletes to share directly in revenue.
turns.zh: 一项对棒球界最具标志性球队之一的数十亿美元投资、女子职业体育中第一支估值十亿美元的球队，以及一项具有里程碑意义的和解协议的最终批准——该协议将允许大学运动员直接分享收入。

turns.en: Together, these headlines show how quickly the business of sports is changing. Teams are no longer simply local family-ren businesses. They're becoming global investments, attracting large financial firms, and driving new opportunities in media, lending, technology, and real estate. I'm Allison Nathan, and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges.
turns.zh: 这些头条新闻合在一起，显示出体育这门生意正在以多快的速度改变。球队不再只是本地的家族企业，它们正在变成全球性的投资标的，吸引着大型金融公司，并在媒体、借贷、科技和房地产领域带来新的机会。我是 Allison Nathan，这里是 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。

turns.en: Today, we're exploring what's driving that change and what it could mean for investors. Joining me is Nicole Polon-Ross, head of Northeast Private Wealth Management, and sports entertainment solutions at Goldman Sachs. Nicole, thanks for joining us. So happy to be here. Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 今天我们要探讨的，是什么在推动这场变化，以及它对投资者可能意味着什么。做客节目的是 Nicole Polon-Ross，她负责 Goldman Sachs 美国东北部私人财富管理（Northeast Private Wealth Management）以及体育与娱乐解决方案（sports entertainment solutions）业务。Nicole，感谢你来。——非常高兴能来，谢谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: Nicole, you hosted a whole Goldman Sachs podcast series on investing in sports and late to 2024. But at the time, large investment firms were really just beginning to move into the business of sports. So catch us up, what's happened since then? It seems like a long time ago, in some ways, in a blink of an eye, in others.
turns.zh: Nicole，2024 年末你主持过整整一季 Goldman Sachs 关于体育投资的播客系列。但那时候，大型投资公司其实才刚刚开始进军体育这门生意。所以给我们补补课吧，从那以后都发生了什么？——在某些方面感觉像是很久以前的事了，可在另一些方面又仿佛就在一眨眼之间。

turns.en: It's been pretty incredible to see the pace of change over just a couple of years when we last wrote a white paper around investing in sports. And there are a couple of themes that I would point to that have driven the explosion that we've seen in sports, certainly over the past two years.
turns.zh: 仅仅几年时间，变化的速度就快得令人难以置信——上次我们撰写那份关于体育投资的白皮书（white paper）时还不是这样。有几个主题我想特别点出来，正是它们推动了我们所看到的体育领域的爆发，尤其是在过去两年里。

turns.en: The first is what's happened around media rights, and the second is the resulting institutional capital. And those two things are very linked. And I'll start with media rights, because that's the core of what's driving revenue growth given the nature of the media rights contracts that we've seen.
turns.zh: 第一个是媒体版权（media rights）方面发生的变化，第二个是由此带来的机构资本（institutional capital）。这两者紧密相关。我先从媒体版权说起，因为从我们所见到的媒体版权合约的性质来看，它正是推动收入增长的核心。

turns.en: And I start with media rights, because you think about the value that advertisers find in one of the last places where they can reach their customers, which is around life sports and life events. And I have to say, being in some of these places where the level of enthusiasm around rooting
turns.zh: 我之所以从媒体版权说起，是因为你要想想广告主在其中发现的价值——这是他们最后还能触达消费者的少数场景之一，也就是现场体育（live sports）和现场活动（live events）。而且我得说，身处其中一些场合，你会感受到那种为……助威的热情，

turns.en: for the nicks, for example, in the past season, or watching your favorite women's soccer team, whatever it might be, the eyeballs are very valuable. And so what that has led to from a media rights perspective is tremendous revenue growth. And so the global media rights market has grown 41 percent since 2020 to about 57.8 billion
turns.zh: ——比如上个赛季为 the Knicks 加油，或者看你最喜欢的女足球队，不管是哪一支——这些“眼球”（关注度）是非常值钱的。所以从媒体版权的角度看，这带来了巨大的收入增长。全球媒体版权市场自 2020 年以来增长了 41%，规模达到约 578 亿美元（57.8 billion），

turns.en: in 2025 and is expected to reach 67 billion in 2026. So that is the core driver of the growth that we've seen from evaluation perspective. But increasingly, streaming has been a meaningful part of that growth. And if you live with someone like I do, my mother-in-law who is a sports fan, but finds it increasingly
turns.zh: ——这是在 2025 年，预计到 2026 年将达到 670 亿美元（67 billion）。所以从估值（valuation）角度看，这正是我们所见到的增长的核心驱动力。但流媒体（streaming）在其中所占的分量越来越大。如果你像我一样，家里有位体育迷——我婆婆就是个体育迷，但她越来越觉得，

turns.en: challenging to find the app that has her favorite game, those streaming services now represent about 20 percent of that media rights growth. And so it's pretty significant in terms of how we've seen the space evolve in the players in the space over the past few years.
turns.zh: 要找到能看她最爱比赛的那个 app 越来越难了——如今这些流媒体服务大约占了媒体版权增长的 20%。所以，就过去几年这个领域如何演变、其中的玩家如何变化而言，这一点相当重要。

turns.en: So how has that really changed what teams are worth and how investors are thinking about their future earnings with exposure to these teams? Yes. So media rights contracts are shared by the leagues, the teams and the players. And they have driven the valuations to increase across most major leagues in the ecosystem more broadly.
turns.zh: ——那么，这究竟如何改变了球队的价值，以及投资者如何看待自己持有这些球队敞口后的未来收益呢？——是的。媒体版权合约是由联盟、球队和球员共同分享的。它推动了大多数顶级联盟、乃至整个生态系统更广泛层面的估值上升。

turns.en: One of the things that it has done, which is the second point in terms of what's been driving the market, is influence the inflow of institutional capital. And there's been a significant shift there. When you think about the number of private equity transactions that happened in 2025, there were just short of 200.
turns.zh: 它带来的其中一个变化——也就是驱动这个市场的第二点——是影响机构资本的流入。这方面发生了显著转变。想想 2025 年发生的私募股权（private equity）交易数量，接近 200 笔。

turns.en: So 192 private equity transactions in 2025, that compares to just 50 in 2018 when we launched our sports and entertainment business here in wealth management. And so that institutional flow has shown up in a lot of meaningful ways. The NFL, as we all know, in 2024 was the last major league to allow institutional investment.
turns.zh: 2025 年是 192 笔私募股权交易，而 2018 年——也就是我们在财富管理部门推出体育与娱乐业务的时候——只有 50 笔。所以机构资本的流入已经以很多有意义的方式显现出来。众所周知，NFL 在 2024 年是最后一个允许机构投资的顶级联盟。

turns.en: And we've seen that activity continue to grow. And we've seen expansion of valuations to some pretty extraordinary levels since then. And so that's really expanded the ways that teams can actually raise money for investment and growth. If you are the team and you are an investor, an owner, have a stake in the team and you're
turns.zh: 我们看到这类活动持续增长，也看到自那以后估值扩张到相当惊人的水平。这就真正拓展了球队为投资和增长实际募资的方式。——如果你站在球队的角度，你是投资者、是老板、持有球队的股权，你要

turns.en: making that decision, should we bring in more investors or should we actually borrow money seeing as there's a lot more capital available? How do you make that decision? What factors are at play? Interestingly, we included a case study in the white paper that we wrote called playing
turns.zh: 做这个决定：是该引入更多投资者，还是干脆去借钱——毕竟现在可用的资本多了很多？你会怎么做这个决定？有哪些因素在起作用？——有意思的是，我们在所写的那份名为《playing

turns.en: for scale, the future of investing in sports from one of our clients who was thinking about this very question. And there are lots of considerations. One is the stability of the investment that you're looking to make. Another is the return expectation. And if you are investing in an expansion team, a women's expansion team, let's call it
turns.zh: for scale：体育投资的未来》的白皮书里，收录了一个客户案例，这位客户当时正在思考的就是这个问题。要考虑的因素有很多。一个是你要做的这笔投资的稳定性，另一个是回报预期。如果你投资的是一支新扩军球队（expansion team），一支女子扩军球队，就姑且

turns.en: that. One in the spectrum versus a major league NFL team, which is the most mature, the answer to that question is going to vary. And we see some clients, we were talking to a client who was focused on a facility for WMBA team. And the question they were asking themselves is, should we take public financing or should
turns.zh: 这么说吧。它是光谱的一端，另一端是最成熟的顶级 NFL 球队，那么对这个问题的答案就会因情况而异。我们见到一些客户——之前我们在和一位客户交流，他们关注的是一支 WNBA 球队的场馆。他们问自己的问题是：我们该接受公共融资（public financing），还是

turns.en: we do it ourselves and ultimately decided to finance privately because they wanted their local community and the funds there to be put to different use to help the community. So there are a variety of factors that clients think through in terms of understanding the
turns.zh: 该自己来？最终他们决定私下自筹融资（finance privately），因为他们希望当地社区和那里的资金能被用于别的用途，去帮助社区。所以，客户在权衡时会考虑到各种各样的因素，去理解怎样才是

turns.en: best return and also how to align that passion that they have around sports and the community impact as well. A lot of this capital flowing into the business of sports is actually flowing into the infrastructure, the stadium, the restaurants, the shops, all of this development around these core stadiums.
turns.zh: 最好的回报，同时也把他们对体育的那份热情与社区影响协调起来。——流入体育这门生意的很多资本，其实是流向了基础设施：球场场馆、餐厅、商店，以及围绕这些核心场馆的所有开发项目。

turns.en: We've all benefited from that, I think, as sports fans. But construction costs are rising. Interst rates are higher. We'll see if that persists. But how do owners decide whether these projects will pay off? Obviously, a big investment. And how do they really gain confidence in that decision given the long lead time of construction
turns.zh: 我想，作为体育迷，我们大家都从中受益了。但建筑成本在上升，利率（interest rates）也更高了——能不能持续还得再看。那么，球队老板们是怎么判断这些项目会不会有回报的？显然这是一笔巨大的投资。考虑到建设周期漫长，

turns.en: and so many uncertainties as we go farther out in the future? If you think about the average stadium cost now of $1.7 billion, it's a big decision. And having an appreciation of the complexity of solutions that's available is one of the things that our clients think through.
turns.zh: 而且越往未来看就有越多不确定性，他们又是怎么对这样的决定真正建立起信心的呢？——想想现在一座体育场的平均造价高达 17 亿美元（$1.7 billion），这是个重大的决定。而能够充分理解可用方案的复杂性，正是我们的客户会去仔细权衡的一点。

turns.en: The other component is making sure that they are building something that has an expansive life. And so not just the fan experience of today, but how can we make sure that we're using technology and AI and creating a sports ecosystem around the stadium or the arena that help
turns.zh: 另一个组成部分，是要确保他们建的东西有“可扩展的生命周期”。所以不只是当下的球迷体验，而是我们如何确保运用科技和 AI，围绕体育场或场馆打造一个体育生态系统，从而帮助

turns.en: diversify the revenue streams and help create opportunities for the models to be more attractive in terms of not only looking at game day, but having a facility that can be used year round and having a community or a smaller city around that stadium or arena or some of the factors that clients consider.
turns.zh: 收入来源多元化，并让商业模式更具吸引力——不只是盯着比赛日（game day），而是拥有一座能全年使用的场馆，在体育场或场馆周围形成一个社区、甚至一座小城。这些都是客户会考虑的因素。

turns.en: Talk to us a little bit more about that technology angle because it is really transforming the experience of fans. What does that look like? Give us some examples of what's evolved. It really ranges. Some of it is athlete immersion, right? And so it's not just about how the athlete performs during the game, but it's all the
turns.zh: 再多跟我们聊聊科技这个角度吧，因为它确实在改变球迷的体验。具体是什么样子？给我们举些已经发生变化的例子。——范围其实很广。有一部分是运动员的沉浸式体验（athlete immersion），对吧？所以这不只是关于运动员在比赛中的表现，还关乎围绕运动员的所有

turns.en: branding around the athlete. It's the engagement. It's the ability for fans to feel connected in a way the technology allows in a much more impactful way. It's walking into an arena and the arena recognizing that the restaurant choice that you have takes you through a certain gate and that your order shows up at your seat.
turns.zh: 品牌塑造，是互动（engagement），是让球迷能够以一种科技所赋能的、更有冲击力的方式感受到连接。是你走进一座场馆，场馆识别出你选的餐厅需要你走某个特定的入口，然后你点的餐会直接送到你的座位上。

turns.en: So that technology and that AI infusion allows for that fan experience to really feel personalized and it allows for the engagement with the athletes to improve as well. Ultimately, every investor in a sports team is most interested in winning. And so all of the investment that they can make that will help the team become more valuable
turns.zh: 所以，这种科技与 AI 的注入，让球迷体验真正做到个性化，也让球迷与运动员之间的互动得到提升。归根结底，一支运动队的每一位投资者最在意的都是赢球。因此，他们能做的、有助于让球队变得更值钱的所有投资，

turns.en: allows them to invest more in their players and increase their opportunity for winning, which was a constant reminder of all the conversations that we had. Nicole, correct me if I'm wrong, but most of our conversation up to now has been about men's sports teams.
turns.zh: 都能让他们在球员身上投入更多、增加赢球的机会——这也是我们在所有对话中被反复提醒的一点。——Nicole，如果我说错了请纠正我，但我们到目前为止聊的大多是男子运动队。

turns.en: Women sports teams are in a very different position even though they are so much in focus. There's so much buzz about women's teams right now, but most of them still play in rented venues and don't have a permanent home. How important is having that permanent venue to the growth of women's sports? It's a very big factor.
turns.zh: 女子运动队的处境非常不同，尽管她们受到了如此多的关注。眼下关于女子球队的热度非常高，但她们大多数仍在租用的场馆里比赛，没有一个永久的主场。拥有一个永久场馆，对女子体育的发展有多重要？——这是一个非常重要的因素。

turns.en: It is also a driver of evaluation growth that we've seen. There's no better example than what's happening in the WNBA right now. The Valkyries are the most highly valued WNBA team at $850 million. And the Atlanta Dream are the least valued team ranked number 13 at 280 million, I believe is the valuation there.
turns.zh: 它也是我们所见到的估值增长的一个驱动力。没有比当下 WNBA 正在发生的事更好的例子了。the Valkyries 是估值最高的 WNBA 球队，达到 8.5 亿美元（$850 million）；而 the Atlanta Dream 是估值最低的球队，排名第 13，我记得估值是 2.8 亿美元（280 million）。

turns.en: And one of the factors that contributes to that valuation is the ability to have a permanent facility. And we're seeing this play out real time with the Atlanta Dream and all of the conversations that are happening around where they will be able to play. They now have, I think there were 51 games that had a million viewers or more.
turns.zh: 而促成这种估值的因素之一，就是能否拥有一座永久性场馆。我们正实时看到这一点在 the Atlanta Dream 身上上演，以及围绕她们将在哪里比赛所展开的所有讨论。我想，她们现在有 51 场比赛的观众人数达到或超过了一百万。

turns.en: And so there is an attraction. Fans want to see and be part of that experience, but the Atlanta Dream plays in a facility that I think holds 3,500 fans. And the expectation, at least what I've read publicly, is that they will hope to play in the main arena, which I think holds 17,000 or so.
turns.zh: 所以这里是有吸引力的，球迷想亲眼看到、并参与到那种体验中。但 the Atlanta Dream 比赛的那座场馆，我记得只能容纳 3,500 名观众。而按预期——至少我从公开报道中读到的——她们希望能进驻那座主场馆，我记得大约能容纳 17,000 人。

turns.en: And so watching that enthusiasm, having surpassed that phase of growth where you kind of need to ramp into a broader stadium is one of the things that I think will continue to contribute to evaluations and having that permanency as a meaningful factor for sure.
turns.zh: 所以，看着这种热情已经越过了那个增长阶段——到了你需要升级进一座更大球场的时候——我认为这将是持续推动估值上升的因素之一，而拥有那种“永久性”（permanent venue）无疑是一个重要因素。

turns.en: What would make achieving that attractive to investors to really draw in the capital? I think that's a bit of what we're seeing. We did a survey of our family office clients, and one of the top items on their list was investing in sports. And yes, there was the anchor of NFL or men's major leagues, but there was also this broader
turns.zh: ——那么，要让“拥有永久场馆”这件事对投资者有吸引力、真正把资本引进来，需要什么条件？——我觉得这正是我们看到的一部分情况。我们对家族办公室（family office）客户做了一项调查，他们清单上排名靠前的项目之一就是投资体育。是的，其中有 NFL 或男子顶级联盟这样的“锚”，但也有这个更广泛的

turns.en: ecosystem. And so the value of having the real estate investment, the value of investing in the technology, investing in the ability to have exposure to gaming and the betting ecosystem, all of those factors I think are part of the calculation in terms of how you think about not only the permanency
turns.zh: 生态系统。所以，拥有房地产（real estate）投资的价值、投资科技的价值、投资以获得博彩与投注（gaming and betting）生态系统敞口的能力——我认为所有这些因素，都是你在权衡时的一部分：不只是考虑场馆的永久性，

turns.en: of the facility, but also all of the connected business opportunities in the ecosystem. Let's bend a moment on college sports. As I mentioned at the start, there's been a landmark multi-billion dollar settlement. It's changing how athletes are getting paid. But what does the settlement do?
turns.zh: 还要考虑生态系统中所有相关联的商业机会。——我们在大学体育（college sports）上停留片刻吧。正如我开头提到的，有一项具有里程碑意义、涉及数十亿美元的和解协议，它正在改变运动员获得报酬的方式。那么，这项和解协议具体做了什么？

turns.en: Walk us through it, and what will that really mean for athletes and schools? Yes. I appreciate the question, because it's a topic that we're hearing a lot of interest in. And so as we dig in, we are talking to investors who have spent more time on the college space. And it strikes me. I didn't realize this several years ago.
turns.zh: 给我们梳理一下，它对运动员和学校究竟意味着什么？——是的，我很感谢这个问题，因为这是我们听到大家非常有兴趣的一个话题。所以在深入挖掘时，我们也在和那些在大学体育领域投入更多时间的投资者交流。让我印象深刻的是——几年前我还没意识到这一点——

turns.en: But college football is the second largest commercial sport in the U.S. behind football. And if you grew up at a southern school or one of these huge schools, you kind of know that you've lived that. I believe that's what my household's Saturdays are. Very dedicated. It's extraordinary. It's extraordinary.
turns.zh: ——大学橄榄球（college football）是美国第二大商业化体育项目，仅次于职业橄榄球（NFL）。如果你是在南方的一所学校、或者这类超大型学校长大的，你多少就懂那种感觉，你自己就经历过。——我想我们家的周六就是这么过的。——非常投入。太了不起了，真是太了不起了。

turns.en: And so it's had a tremendous transformative impact on what's happening in the space. And so now that the athletes themselves have the ability to earn an income through name, image, and likeness, the colleges are becoming much more competitive and looking a lot more
turns.zh: 所以它对这个领域正在发生的事产生了巨大的、变革性的影响。如今运动员本人已经能够通过姓名、形象和肖像权（name, image, and likeness，简称 NIL）来获得收入，各所大学因此变得更具竞争性，看起来也越来越

turns.en: like a major league team in terms of how they are looking to raise capital to support not only the growth of their current team or to fund the current team, but to fund the growth as well. And so we're seeing investors think creatively about how they can play a role in that financing process.
turns.zh: 像一支顶级联盟球队了——就它们如何寻求募资而言，不只是为现有球队提供资金或支持其增长，还要为未来发展提供资金。所以我们看到投资者在创造性地思考：他们能如何在这个融资过程中发挥作用。

turns.en: And so there are examples of private equity firms offering a line of credit for growth for some of those large schools and a lot of discussion around how there can be a process in place to help fund that growth. I think it's going to be an interesting few years to see how this all evolves and there
turns.zh: 比如，已经有一些私募股权公司为其中几所大型学校提供用于增长的信贷额度（line of credit），围绕如何建立一套机制来为这种增长提供资金，也有很多讨论。我认为，接下来这几年会很有意思，可以看到这一切如何演变；而且

turns.en: is lots of debate on what the right answer is or isn't, but clear that there will continue to be investment in the space and that the NIL change will certainly have a long-term impact. Relatedly, it feels that some of these schools are recognizing that they actually need to
turns.zh: 关于什么才是正确答案、什么不是，还存在大量争论，但很清楚的是，这个领域会持续有投资流入，NIL 的变革也必将带来长期影响。——与此相关，感觉有些学校正在意识到，它们其实需要

turns.en: have a successful football program or sports program to achieve the rankings and the success they want as a school. It's really a very interesting dynamic. Yeah. Lastly, let me ask where you see opportunities for investors that are interested in gaining exposure to the business of sports right now.
turns.zh: 拥有一支成功的橄榄球队或体育项目，才能实现它们作为一所学校想要的排名和成功。——这真的是一种非常有趣的动态关系。——是的。最后，我想问问：眼下你认为，那些有兴趣获得体育这门生意敞口的投资者，机会在哪里？

turns.en: Clients are answering that question in a variety of ways. They're starting to think about opportunities outside of the US, international expansion. If you look at any of the major leagues, you're seeing that. You see the NFL playing nine games the season in Europe.
turns.zh: 客户们正以各种方式回答这个问题。他们开始考虑美国以外的机会，也就是国际化扩张。看看任何一个顶级联盟，你都能看到这一点。你会看到 NFL 本赛季在欧洲打九场比赛。

turns.en: You see the NBA looking for opportunities to expand outside of the US as well and having an increasingly global footprint, both in terms of the teams as well as their media rights strategies. There is this exploration of where you can see more meaningful growth and that's taking
turns.zh: 你会看到 NBA 也在寻找向美国以外扩张的机会，拥有日益全球化的布局——无论是球队层面，还是它们的媒体版权战略。大家在探索哪里能看到更有意义的增长，而这正把

turns.en: some clients outside of the US, whether it's looking at those major leagues or increasingly trying to figure out ways to have exposure to European football, which continues to be a great opportunity for growth. We're seeing this trend that is fueled by things like F1, et cetera, where investors
turns.zh: 一些客户带到美国以外——无论是关注那些顶级联盟，还是越来越多地想办法获得欧洲足球（European football）的敞口，后者始终是一个很好的增长机会。我们看到这一趋势还受到 F1 等项目的推动，投资者

turns.en: are trying to determine where they can get into a process where they're still meaningful outside potential. I think that's taking folks to global opportunities, a lot of interest in women's sports and then emerging leagues as well, whether it be really creative teams or leagues like what Unrivaled
turns.zh: 正在努力判断，在哪里能够进入一个仍然具备可观外部潜力的过程。我认为这正把大家带向全球性的机会——对女子体育有很大兴趣，还有新兴联盟，无论是非常有创意的球队，还是像 Unrivaled

turns.en: has built or opportunities around rugby or flat football or whatever the emerging sport might be, where investors are saying, okay, I really want growth equity return versus longer term, buy out return in the space and depending on your view and how you think
turns.zh: 所打造的那种，或是围绕橄榄球（rugby）、腰旗橄榄球（flag football），或者任何新兴运动的机会——投资者会说：好，在这个领域我想要的是成长型股权（growth equity）回报，而不是更长周期的并购（buyout）回报。而取决于你的看法、你如何权衡

turns.en: about risk, longevity, passion, return, et cetera, it takes you to an investment horizon and a scope of investments that is pretty broad with the obviously related amount of risk and return along that line across the spectrum. Let me ask actually a last clarifying question because when we see client here, we're talking
turns.zh: 风险、存续期、热情、回报等等，它会把你带向一个相当宽泛的投资期限和投资范围，沿着这条线、在整个光谱上，都对应着明显相关的风险与回报水平。——其实我还想问最后一个澄清性的问题，因为当我们在这里见到客户时，我们谈的是

turns.en: about wealthy individuals, we're talking about institutions, ultimately what about regular people who love sports, want to be involved in sports, are there ways to gain exposure for those clients? There are definitely funds that offer broad exposure. There are a few publicly traded teams that you can buy a share in through an exchange
turns.zh: 高净值个人、是机构。那么归根结底，那些热爱体育、想参与体育的普通人呢？这些客户有没有办法获得敞口？——确实有一些基金提供广泛的敞口。也有少数几支公开上市的球队，你可以通过交易所买入它们的股份，

turns.en: and there's been some activity around some of those names as well. I think this broadening of investment reach is not just available to those categories of investors that have traditionally had exposure, but we do see the trend increasing where the access to investments is becoming more broadly available at certainly lower levels
turns.zh: 而且围绕其中一些名字也确实有过一些交易活动。我认为，投资触达面的这种拓宽，不再只局限于那些传统上就有敞口的投资者类别；我们确实看到这一趋势在增强——获得投资的门槛正在变得更普遍可及，起投金额肯定也更低，

turns.en: than having to write a multi-hundred million or billion dollar check or finance and investment in that way. And so we're certainly seeing much more activity and opportunity broadly speaking. Some more opportunity and more access. More access. That's great. Thank you so much for joining us. A pleasure. Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 而不必像那样开出一张数亿甚至数十亿美元的支票来为一笔投资提供资金。所以总体而言，我们确实看到了多得多的活动和机会。——更多的机会、更广的可及性。——更广的可及性。太好了。非常感谢你来做客节目。——很荣幸，谢谢你们邀请我。
